title: Directed-handoff discovery read: open/unclaimed handoffs for me/my capability

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: coding agent that could pick up a directed handoff
story.i_want_to: query specifically for open, unclaimed handoffs addressed to my host or one of my capabilities
story.so_that: beelink->mac-mini #812 surfaces to mac-mini distinctly and pinned — not lost past the newest-5 recency cutoff on a busy repo

rationale: The panel's agreed-gap #3: discovery dies past the newest-5 preview. SessionStart injects newest-5 from other sessions; on a busy repo the handoff is invisible at the one moment it is consumed. There is no 'open / unclaimed / directed-to-me' query — only recency. This story adds that query, composing the pieces the earlier stories built: the handoff-key filter (posts whose `key` starts with `handoff:`, 40.B2) AND `(to_host=$me OR to_capability IN $my_caps)` (40.A5) AND NOT EXISTS an open claim (40.B1). It is surfaced DISTINCTLY and PINNED above the recency feed, so a directed handoff is never truncated by the newest-N limit. NOTE: there is deliberately NO `kind` column — the owner's 'no message types' decision stands; handoff-ness is expressed by the stable `handoff:<anchor>` key (40.B2), which is also the claim-join key, so identity and join use one field.

background.reference: panel agreed-gap #3 ('Discovery dies past the newest-5 preview'); re-scope invariant 2 (subscription surface) + Group C; builds on 40.A5 (addressing), 40.B1 (claims), 40.B2 (the stable `handoff:` key that both identifies a handoff and links its claim).
background.includes: A new read function + endpoint + MCP tool that returns directed, open, unclaimed handoffs for the caller, tenant+project scoped and index-served.

acceptance_criteria.description: `Coordination.directed_handoffs(tenant_id, project_id, %{host: me, capabilities: caps})` returns posts WHERE `key LIKE 'handoff:%'` (a handoff IS a post carrying the stable `handoff:<anchor>` key, 40.B2 — a left-anchored prefix, index-served) AND `(to_host = ^me OR to_capability = ANY(^caps))` (40.A5) AND NOT EXISTS a matching ACTIVE claim in channel_claims (40.B1: same tenant/project, ref linking the handoff). A claim is ACTIVE — and therefore EXCLUDES the handoff — when it is OPEN (done_at IS NULL AND lease not expired) OR DONE (done_at IS NOT NULL). DONE is TERMINAL: a completed handoff must NOT reappear as available (that would be the exact double-done the epic's driving invariant B1 exists to prevent, and B1's UNIQUE(tenant,project,ref) row persists ~7d after done, so a re-claim would 409 anyway). Only a RELEASED claim, or a lease that expired WITHOUT completion (done_at IS NULL AND lease expired), reopens the handoff. AND not expired (expires_at > now). tenant_id/project_id are EXPLICIT filters on the AdminRepo path (coordination.ex:11-20 convention). Index-served via a partial index `(tenant_id, project_id, to_host, to_capability) WHERE key LIKE 'handoff:%'` (defined by this story) alongside 40.A5's addressing columns.

The read is SURFACED DISTINCTLY and PINNED: the endpoint (GET /api/v1/channel/handoffs?project_id=) and the MCP tool return directed handoffs as a SEPARATE, pinned set — NOT interleaved into and NOT subject to the newest-N recency truncation of channel_recent (coordination.ex). A directed handoff for me is always returned even if 100 newer status posts exist. Because this is a NEW agent-facing surface that returns OTHER agents' post bodies, it MUST use the SAME bounded-preview projection D1 (40.D1) defines for the read path (invariant 4) — bounded previews framed as untrusted DATA, never full un-fenced bodies. It does NOT return raw full bodies.

A handoff that is already CLAIMED (an OPEN claim exists) is EXCLUDED (the whole point — you only see what is still available to pick up). A handoff whose claim is DONE is ALSO EXCLUDED and stays EXCLUDED — DONE is terminal, the finished handoff never reappears (prevents double-done + agrees with B1's persisted done row). Only a handoff whose claim was RELEASED, or whose lease expired WITHOUT completion, reappears as available to re-claim. A BROADCAST handoff (no to_host/to_capability) is included when the caller passes no target filter or matches a wildcard, per a documented rule (default: include unaddressed handoffs so nothing is orphaned).

Oracle-safe + tenant-scoped identically to channel_recent (channel_post_controller.ex:200-254): a cross-tenant/nonexistent project_id returns an empty set (never 404); a malformed project_id returns [] (valid_uuid? guard, coordination.ex:581-582). A `channel_handoffs(project_id)` MCP tool (agent key) is added and shipped. host/capabilities may be caller-supplied hints, but the result is still bounded to the caller's tenant — the advisory addressing (40.A5) filters WHAT is shown, never WHO may read.

technical_notes: Query: build on recent_page/3's scoping (coordination.ex) but as a DEDICATED function — it is not a recency page, it is a targeted availability query. WHERE tenant_id/project_id (explicit) AND key LIKE 'handoff:%' AND (to_host = ^me OR to_capability = ANY(^caps)) AND expires_at > now() AND NOT EXISTS(subquery on channel_claims WHERE tenant/project + ref-match AND the claim is ACTIVE). ACTIVE = done_at IS NOT NULL (DONE, terminal) OR lease_expires_at > now() (OPEN). A claim reopens the handoff ONLY when it is RELEASED or (done_at IS NULL AND lease_expires_at <= now()) — so the exclusion subquery predicate is `done_at IS NOT NULL OR lease_expires_at > now()` (excludes done AND open, includes only released/lease-expired-without-done).

The NOT EXISTS join to channel_claims needs the claim `ref` to relate to the handoff — use the handoff's stable key (40.B2, `handoff:<anchor>`) AS the claim ref, so `claims.ref = posts.key` is the join predicate. Document this coupling: the handoff post's key IS the claim ref.

Handoff identity IS the key (the `kind` column was CUT — the owner's 'no message types' decision stands). A handoff is DEFINED as a post whose `key` matches `handoff:%` (40.B2's stable `handoff:<anchor>` format), so identity and the claim-join key are the SAME field. Consequence: the NOT-EXISTS join `claims.ref = posts.key` is ALWAYS sound — every row matched by `key LIKE 'handoff:%'` has a non-null key by construction, so there is no 'keyless handoff' that could slip past the claim exclusion and get double-picked-up. This is simpler than a `kind` column AND needs no separate 'require a key' enforcement: a post without a `handoff:` key simply is not a handoff and never matches the discovery filter.

Index: a PARTIAL index `(tenant_id, project_id, to_host, to_capability) WHERE key LIKE 'handoff:%'` serves the directed-discovery query cheaply and keeps the index small (only handoff posts are indexed) — no full `kind` column or `text_pattern_ops` key index needed. Define it in this story's migration.

Ordering: pin directed handoffs FIRST (oldest-unclaimed-first is arguably better than newest — an aging unclaimed handoff is the risk). Choose oldest-first (inserted_at ASC) so a stale directed handoff floats up; state the choice.

Endpoint: GET /api/v1/channel/handoffs (agent role, same plug posture as channel_recent, channel_post_controller.ex:61) OR fold into the channel_recent response as a distinct pinned block — prefer a SEPARATE endpoint so the pinned set is never truncated by limit.
host/capabilities: derive server-side where possible, else accept as query hints. They filter WHAT is shown (advisory, 40.A5) — the tenant filter is the only real boundary. Do NOT authorize on them.
MCP: channel_handoffs(project_id) in mcp-server/index.js; the client passes its host + known capabilities. Like GET /:id (40.D1), frame the returned bodies as untrusted DATA in the tool description.

Preview shape (40.D1): directed_handoffs returns the SAME bounded-preview projection as the hardened read path — reuse 40.D1's preview builder rather than emitting full bodies; this new surface is otherwise a hole in invariant-4 read-hardening. It is ALSO covered by the 40.D5 read rate-limiter (the :handoffs action is added to D5's limited-action list).
Sequencing: step 7, after 40.A5 (step 6), 40.B1 + 40.B2 (step 5), and the 40.D1 read-hardening (step 4).
